project_profile.composition: DOM UI with an app-owned canvas scene behind a navigation overlay
project_profile.minimum_target: Modern browsers, with browser and GPU feature support varying by device
project_profile.backdrop_access: The application can render its own scene into a canvas; arbitrary DOM and cross-origin images are not assumed to be sampleable
project_profile.graphics: WebGL2 is an available candidate; WebGPU availability must be detected at runtime

task: Implement a refractive navigation pill with crisp icons and an attached search bubble that can grow and reconnect smoothly.
must_discover: browser feature support and minimum browser expectations
canvas origin cleanliness and cross-origin asset constraints
whether the real backdrop is owned by the application render pipeline
DOM stacking, clipping, resize, and device-pixel-ratio behavior
semantic navigation, focus, keyboard, and reduced-motion behavior
must_consider: canvas/GPU composition for actual backdrop displacement when the app-owned scene is available
WebGL2 versus WebGPU only after feature detection and compatibility checks
DOM semantic controls layered above the optical surface
a documented blur/translucency fallback when backdrop pixels cannot be sampled
must_not_assume: WebGPU exists on every supported browser or device
arbitrary DOM pixels can be used as a shader texture
cross-origin images can be read without origin-clean handling
CSS backdrop blur is equivalent to refraction

workflow.required_output: React/TypeScript, browser targets, canvas ownership, origin constraints, and existing build/test commands
pill and attached-lobe silhouette, backdrop displacement, stable icon semantics, and merge/reconnect states
compare WebGL2, detected WebGPU, DOM/native effects, and fallback; justify one primary path
canvas optical layer plus semantic DOM overlay, capability gates, clipping, coordinate mapping, and fallback
incremental surface, mask/distortion, material response, and interruptible lobe motion
build/tests, feature-gate checks, bright/dark/detailed backdrops, keyboard/focus, reduced motion, and frame-cost review
changed files, actual tests, demonstrated fidelity tier, limitations, and visual evidence

acceptance: No unverified browser/GPU feature is selected as a universal dependency
Backdrop distortion is only claimed when the controlled scene is actually displaced
The DOM remains responsible for semantic labels and interactive navigation
Fallback is reported as L0/L1 rather than L2/L3 when it only blurs or tints
